newsitem.title: FRANCE: Poland favours wider NATO enlargement.
newsitem.headline: Poland favours wider NATO enlargement.

text.p: Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, differing with the United States, said on Wednesday the enlargement of NATO should not be limited to a handful of countries invited to join next month.

Addressing the Council of Europe's parliamentary assembly, he said the admission of Poland, the Czech Republic and Hungary, expected to be formally launched at a NATO summit in Madrid, should be only a first step.
"If we understand the arguments of those who wish the enlargement of NATO to be limited, we do not think that is logical," Cimoszewicz said.
"Poland's accession will only be a first step," he added.
President Bill Clinton angered several European allies earlier this month by announcing unilaterally that the United States would only support the entry of three new members in the first phase.
A majority of European allies, led by France and Italy, want Romania and Slovenia to be included in the first wave as well.

Clinton said after a weekend Group of Seven summit in Denver that differences remained with European partners over which countries should be asked to join NATO, but he did not believe this would damage the alliance.

Diplomats said the Europeans still hoped the United States would at least agree that all five countries were allowed to start negotiations from the same "starting line", even if it was made clear that only three were likely to be admitted in a first intake in 1999.
